manual_adjustments: Two concurrent S3 control-plane writes returned OperationAborted immediately after bucket creation; encryption and tagging were retried serially and verified.
The repository-scoped IAM policy was expanded from ECR pull-only to push-and-pull so the workbench can publish the digest-pinned image.
An encrypted SQS sink was added after the new SNS topic was observed to have zero consumers; an end-to-end test message was received and then purged.

Pre-launch review found that the worker's encryption boundary check needed s3:GetEncryptionConfiguration; the bucket-scoped permission was added to the live inline role policy and policy simulation returned allowed.

Pre-launch review found that the instance role could not pull the pinned cross-account AWS DLC; exact-repository ECR pull permissions were added for 763104351884/pytorch-training while push remains restricted to the project repository.
The first workbench launch added a one-time EventBridge Scheduler stop deadline outside the guest and retained the guest systemd timer as defense in depth.
Live storage discovery found the DLAMI-managed LVM/ext4 instance store at /opt/dlami/nvme; workers must reuse that mount and must not format the device.

Camera-enabled startup in the untouched Isaac Lab 2.2.0 base reproduced the NVIDIA-known Isaac Sim RTX crash on base AMI ami-01901bc01d5d9bb55 with driver 595.71.05, while non-camera startup succeeded. Evaluation launches are therefore pinned to amazon-owned ami-06517bc7fad3c6a48 (Ubuntu 22.04, NVIDIA driver 580.126.09).

RoboLab dependency resolution selected typing-extensions 4.16.0 and typeguard 4.6.0, breaking the bundled Torch 2.7.0 import path; the image was rebuilt with typeguard 4.4.2 and typing_extensions 4.12.2 and now proves both imports during build.
Host-side ECR verification required ecr:DescribeImages; the action was added only for the project repository, applied live, simulated as allowed, and verified without replacing the workbench.
The first paid evaluator on the R580 AMI passed all 128 upstream camera/task smoke tests, wrote a versioned evidence log with smoke_exit_code=0, and self-terminated.
The workbench staging environment lacked polars; the frozen-lock version 1.30.0 was installed in place before the DROID parquet validation.

The first real DROID gate exposed that LeRobot v3 video features live in MP4 subtrees referenced by episode metadata rather than data-parquet columns; the validator was corrected against the pinned snapshot before accepting any manifest.

The exact 1 TiB workbench gp3 volume was increased in place from 125 to 500 MiB/s during large integrity hashing; it remains scheduled for termination with the workbench and the bounded added throughput cost stays inside the non-compute reserve.

The final episode-derived DROID validator passed exact schema, parquet, video-reference, timestamp, file-count, and byte-count gates before a versioned S3 upload; an independent version-specific manifest fetch and payload listing reproduced its hash and totals.
